name: Ali Khamenei
summary: Khamenei led Iran as Supreme Leader for 37 years under the doctrine of clerical guardianship, defending an Islamic republic he called religious democracy against Western liberal models. He combined support for privatization and self-reliance with state control of culture and dissent, conservative views on gender and family, and fierce opposition to the United States and Israel. He backed civilian nuclear work while reportedly forbidding nuclear weapons by fatwa.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pushed privatization (2007, Article 44) and criticized unnecessary state interference, while also favouring a state-guided resistance economy and self-reliance.

property-fundamental.rationale: Suggested courts protect ownership rights to encourage private investment (2007).

strong-leader.rationale: Expanded the Leader's control over state institutions and said power must be used rather than wasted.

empower-police-military.rationale: Built up the IRGC as an instrument of domestic control and regional influence.

traditional-family.rationale: Backed pronatalist policy, gender segregation and criticized Western treatment of women and family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Described homosexuality as a moral deprivation found in the West.

more-religion-public.rationale: Led a state built on Islamic principles in public life and praised religious democracy as still attractive when liberal democracy had lost appeal (2006).

gender-social-construct.rationale: Described gender equality as a plot to corrupt women's role in society, implying distinct natural roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Warned against Western cultural influence and praised Persian as the language of revolutionary Islam.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Supported civilian nuclear technology and endorsed the 2015 nuclear deal.

democracy-best.rationale: Called elections a pivot of religious democracy but argued liberal democracy had lost its appeal and the Guardian Council he oversaw disqualified many candidates; position is mixed.

separate-church-state.rationale: Rejected the Western liberal model in favour of religious democracy and ran a system fusing clerical and state authority.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Presided over a system where laws must conform to Islamic criteria and the Guardian Council can veto bills on that ground (Arts. 4, 91, 96); defended it as religious democracy.

limit-population.rationale: Called for rising population and opposed measures to reduce it (see pronatalist policy reported in the opened article).

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Called Israel a 'brutal Zionist regime', a 'cancerous tumor' and said it would not exist in 25 years.

dominated-front.rationale: Cast the US as the leading force of imperialism, opposed Western dominance, and rejected talks with Washington (Feb 2025).

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Believed in gender segregation and called equality a plot to corrupt women's role, while stating women may take part in political and social life.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Called for using oil and gas reserves to make Iran an energy superpower (2007), though he also criticized oil dependence.

national-mission.rationale: His foreign policy centred on exporting the Islamic revolution; he framed the Arab Spring as an Islamic awakening.

party-controls-media.rationale: Controlled media through his office's influence and blocked a 2000 press-law reform; critics report persecution for insulting the leader.

clerical-rule.rationale: As Supreme Leader he held the highest political authority as the qualified jurist under velayat-e faqih (constitution Arts. 5, 109, 113).

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Issued a 1996 fatwa against promoting music in schools and urged poetry to serve the revolution.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Reportedly issued a fatwa forbidding production, stockpiling and use of nuclear weapons, cited by Iran at the IAEA in 2005; its status is questioned by some experts.

women-must-cover.rationale: Defended compulsory hijab as honouring women and answered Western objections to it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Promoted self-reliance and a resistance economy, urged domestic production and warned against making the economy dependent on sanctions relief.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said religious democracy derived from Islamic doctrine is distinct from, and more attractive than, Western liberal democracy.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Backed the Axis of Resistance and hosted Hamas leaders, praising their struggle (Feb 2025).

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Reversed his earlier acceptance of birth control and backed population-growth policy; Iran adopted childbirth incentives. Only a caption in the opened article attributes the 150 million target to him.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Referred to 'the myth of the massacre of Jews' (2006) and said in 2014 that the Holocaust's reality was uncertain; Iran's foreign minister later said remarks were mistranslated. Contested.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Sidelined leftist factions, moderate clerics and dissidents; protests in 2009, 2017-19, 2022-23 were repressed under his rule; urged judges to crack down on dissent.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Defended the constitutional order in which sovereignty belongs to God (Art. 56) and contrasted religious democracy with liberal democracy.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Ordered the National Information Network and set up the Supreme Council of Cyberspace; opposed unbridled internet access. Interpretation of shutdowns is partly the cited author's.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said women may take part in political, cultural and social life and called denying them education or choice in marriage oppression; female suffrage continued under him.

notes: Khamenei died on 28 February 2026 (Wikipedia). No answer is marked Inferred: each rests on stated views or record as reported in the opened sources. Many themes (taxation, welfare, ecology, technology, most institutional design questions) are null because no reliable position was found in opened sources. Holocaust remarks are contested (mistranslation claim). Opened sources are mostly secondary reports of his speeches; khamenei.ir could not be fetched.
